(3) Identify maximum noise levels that are acceptable on the public lands, and establish procedures for monitoring noise levels and enforcing a ban on excessively noisy vehicles.
(4) Set up the procedures and studies that are necessary to determine areas of 
(a) Low use by recreational interests other than ORVs, where ORVs might conflict minimally with other users of public lands.
(b) Ecological fragility, unstable soils, or other features that might make ORV use unacceptably destructive.
(5) Provide, to the extent possible with existing knowledge, detailed use criteria for ORVs. ORVs should be classified according to size, weight, power, and special features, such as tires or mufflers, that will have environmental impacts. Use criteria should then relate these classes to the different terrain, biological communities, and climates where ORVs may be used.
The new Draft Statement should identify as precisely as possible the environmental impacts of the use levels and criteria set by the Secretary. It should refer to the information currently available on ORV impacts, and should attempt to point out where further studies need to be done. Only in this way can it serve as a meaningful guide to understanding the Secretary's action and to formulating future policies.
In order to facilitate public comment, the Secretary should also hold hearings on the new Draft Statement.
